parents.title: For Parents
parents.pitch: A rollicking Wild West adventure built for reading aloud — packed with real history, real Australian wildlife, and seven unforgettable characters.
parents.theme1Body: Seven genuine possum species from Down Under. Kids walk away knowing a Honey Possum from a Greater Glider — and asking to learn more.
parents.theme2Body: The 1873 California shipwreck, the cross-country journey east, and real frontier geography woven naturally into every chapter.
parents.theme3Body: The Posse bickers, disagrees, and drives each other crazy — then saves the day anyway. A natural conversation-starter about working through conflict.
parents.theme4Body: Available in English, Mexican Spanish, and Brazilian Portuguese. A perfect pick for multilingual families and bilingual classrooms.
parents.frontierTitle: The Frontier Post: Your Reading Companion
parents.frontierBody: The adventure doesn't stop at the last page. The Frontier Post delivers real possum facts, Wild West history dispatches, and family activities — everything you need to keep the conversation going long after story time.
parents.niloraNote: A note from Nilora: I know what you're thinking — why take a book recommendation from a dog? Fair question. But as a reformed possum-chaser with a reputation for thoroughness, I did my research. These seven are the real deal.

author.title: About the Author
author.intro1: Hello. I am Nilora Takia. I realize my name might sound a bit “exotic” to those of you who walk on two legs, but in the world of four-legged intellectuals, I assure you it is quite a classic.
author.intro2: I am an aspiring author. Currently, I am writing a book for “little humans” about Australian possums. Now, I know what you’re thinking: “Nilora, why would a dog write a book about her sworn enemies?” It’s a fair question. Usually, my relationship with marsupials involves a lot of barking and chasing them off my lawn. There is one particular possum in my backyard who refuses to leave, no matter how much I “discuss” the matter with her through the fence. Oh, what I wouldn’t give for just one little nip!
author.introQuestion: So, why write about the very creatures I find so annoying?
author.discovery1: It all started with my two pets. There’s Daddy (the tall one) and Sweetheart (the smaller, faster one). They were looking at an old digital newspaper from the 1800s. They were researching a famous train robbery in the Wild West—California, to be exact.
author.discovery2: According to the article, a group of bandits had boarded the “Iron Bronco” (that’s what they called trains back then). But here’s the weird part: the bandits’ “perfect plan” fell apart before they could even steal a single gold coin. Nobody knew why!
author.discovery3: I leaned in to look at the blurry, black-and-white photo of the crime scene. At first, I thought I saw a very strange-looking cat. But I sniffed the screen, looked closer, and gasped.
author.discovery4: Standing right there in the middle of the desert was a White Lemur Possum. A rare Hemibelideus lemuroides, to be scientific. I was flabbergasted! What was an Australian possum doing in the American Southwest in the 19th century?
author.legend1: I did some digging (and I don’t mean in the garden). I discovered a hidden legend: The Awesome Aussie Possum Posse.
author.legend2: It turns out a small group of Australian possums actually saved the Wild West! They protected the frontier from a greedy gang of goons who were trying to take over. Their story was so brave—so inspiring—that I couldn’t believe it had been forgotten.
author.legend3: It is a historical tragedy! And as a dog of great honor, I plan to fix it. I am writing a glorious tribute to these marvelous marsupials. It’s time the world knew the truth about the heroes from Down Under.

illustrator.title: About the Illustrator
illustrator.para1: Arthur Nascimento, known as Tucco Nascimento, is a Brazilian illustrator with a passion for art that began in childhood. Born in São Paulo, he started drawing at a very young age and has since developed his skills into a career dedicated to bringing stories to life through visual storytelling. His work is recognized for its ability to transform ideas into engaging and emotional scenes, creating a deep connection with readers.
illustrator.para2: His artistic style is versatile, with a strong focus on children's illustration and character design. Tucco draws inspiration from storytelling itself, aiming to convey emotion, movement, and personality in every piece, always with an expressive and captivating touch. As a freelance illustrator, he has worked on book projects, editorial illustrations, and personal creations, demonstrating his ability to adapt his style to different stories and audiences.
illustrator.para3: In this particular project, Tucco felt a strong connection from the very beginning. The humor, action, and dynamic pace of the story align perfectly with the kind of illustrations he most enjoys creating. Each scene was carefully crafted to enhance the rhythm of the narrative, highlighting expressions, movement, and key moments that make the experience more immersive. His goal was not only to illustrate the story, but to expand it, helping the reader feel closer to the characters and fully engaged in the adventure.
illustrator.para4: Driven by curiosity and imagination, Tucco is constantly exploring new ideas and ways to grow as an artist. His dedication and attention to detail ensure that every project carries a unique identity, full of personality and passion.
illustrator.linksTitle: You can explore more of his work and get in touch through the links below:
illustrator.quote: I'm sure you won't regret embarking on this adventure, and I hope my illustrations take you on a journey, sparking your imagination and bringing this story even more vividly to life.

character.sectionSubtitle: Seven extraordinary Aussie possums who rode into legend

brennen.name: Brennen
brennen.blurb: Brennen has a gift for showing up exactly when someone's in trouble — cool, charming, and born to lead. His mission: round up his friends and find his way back home to Australia.

gretel.name: Gretel
gretel.blurb: Don't mistake Gretel for a damsel in distress — this greater glider solves problems before anyone else spots them. Her gliding membranes let her swoop in like a kite and save the day in style.

hana.name: Hanna
hana.blurb: Don't let the tiny size fool you — Hanna is barely the size of a thimble, but she's sharp, sneaky, and nimble. Need a contraption to save the townsfolk? She'll have it built before you finish asking.

plaid.name: Plaid
plaid.blurb: Plaid isn't much for small talk and he won't be winning any fashion contests. But when you're stuck in a tight spot, he's exactly who you want — wild animals follow wherever he goes.

pygmy.name: Pygmy
pygmy.blurb: Don't be fooled by the tiny frame — Pygmy's tail stretches a full city block and hits like a charging rhino. He's the gentlest soul in the Posse, but cross the wrong line and you'll find yourself launched over the moon.

remmy.name: Remmy
remmy.blurb: Remmy just wants to have a jolly good time — bad guys always make the mistake of underestimating him. Stare at those wall eyes a moment too long and you've been 'Whamied,' ready to do whatever Remmy says.

willow.name: Willow
willow.blurb: Willow Willemina is a white ringtail possum with a fiery streak and zero fear. No villain too tough, no brawl too big — if roughians are giving you trouble, Willow's already on her way.
